route_status.proven_scope: The unchanged probe instantiates bathroom cleanup state, feeds synthetic screen touch/drag events and scripted gesture points, and asserts partial fixture reveal, one-finger ownership, release, focus cancellation, lifted-stroke progress, and completion thresholds. It verifies the bathroom scrub mechanic under Godot 4.7.2 headless.
route_status.gaps: The probe directly calls setup with announcements disabled and directly invokes gesture handlers/probe seams. It does not establish the fresh-save visible route into the bathroom, ordinary production input routing on a rendered display, actual voice playback, or the clean-phone visual/tactile result. No target-device, child, or owner observation occurred.

source_constants.value: Sink scrub requires at least 1.5 seconds of valid motion, 520 px accumulated travel, and 1.05 turns of arc; its configured gesture window is 1.5–5.0 seconds.
Tub scrub requires at least 1.5 seconds of valid motion, 520 px travel, and two direction reversals; its configured gesture window is 1.5–5.0 seconds.
The probe passes three 0.8-second sink motion segments separated by 0.5-second lifts, and asserts the gesture completes.

timing.assumptions: No child session duration is inferred. The probe's segment durations and runner wall time are not observed play duration.

tactile.target_size: The gesture surface covers the 1280×720 base canvas (scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleaning.gd:476-483); sink press start is accepted within 314 px of its center, and tub press start within the configured horizontal band (scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleaning.gd:322-330). These are source geometry only; projected phone hit area and comfort were not measured.
tactile.press_response: A valid sink drag moves the sponge with the touch and emits a sink scrub segment; the fixture mask is updated on changed pixels (scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleaning.gd:613-635; scripts/games/day_one_fixture_scrub.gd:46-70). The headless probe observes local reveal values, not a rendered response-time measurement.
tactile.drag_hold_release: Dragging accumulates sink arc/distance or tub distance/reversals. A stationary hold cannot finish. Finger release ends the active gesture while preserving accumulated counters and visible scrub marks; focus loss clears ownership and cancels the active gesture (scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleaning.gd:351-365,575-590). Probe asserts these scripted behaviors, including lifted strokes.
tactile.ownership: The first touch ID owns the gesture until release; another finger ID is ignored (scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleaning.gd:548-572). The probe asserts second-finger rejection, but the input is delivered through test calls rather than a physical phone session.
tactile.cancellation: Release clears a press buffered while the sponge travels; a still-held press begins after travel completes. Focus-loss cancellation clears touch ownership and does not erase already visible partial mask progress (scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleaning.gd:585-602; probe.log:34-41,70-73).

play_appeal.hypothesis: A sponge that follows the finger while dirt clears along its path can give a direct cause-and-effect scrub. Preserved progress across brief lifts may make a wobbly, stop-start motion forgiving; the sink circle and tub back-and-forth ask for two distinct motions. Whether those cues feel satisfying or understandable to a child remains unobserved.

observations.title: Partial dirt reveal follows the scrub path and remains local
evidence: scripts/games/day_one_fixture_scrub.gd:46-70 (segment mask draws a bounded brush path and updates its texture)
scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleaning.gd:627-630 (moved sink tool emits the exact previous-to-current segment)

scripts/probe_day_one_bathroom_cleanup.gd:215-232; audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L03/attempt_1/probe.log:42-46 (probe observes reveal on the scrubbed region, untouched pixels remain dirty, and progress remains incomplete)
observations.reproduction: Run the focused probe once; its synthetic sink drag creates mask marks and checks reveal_at on a touched and untouched source point. Receipt records PASS with zero failure lines.
observations.child_impact: The local visible state change is tied to the scrub path and does not claim the whole fixture is clean early. Actual on-screen legibility and two-frame response were not measured headlessly.
observations.proposed_repair: No code repair indicated by this evidence. Review the same partial and completed states in a rendered Mobile capture and on the target phone.
observations.acceptance_test: On the target phone, make a short routed scrub and verify dirt visibly clears exactly under the tool within the response budget, untouched dirt remains visible, and full cleanliness appears only after the intended gesture gate.

observations.title: Brief lifts preserve accumulated scrub effort
evidence: scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleaning.gd:351-355 (gesture release ends active motion without resetting scrub counters)

scripts/probe_day_one_bathroom_cleanup.gd:348-366; audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L03/attempt_1/probe.log:62-69 (three 0.8-second sink touches with 0.5-second lifts complete the scripted gesture)
observations.reproduction: The focused probe issues successive sink gestures with simulated motion durations and calls probe_end_gesture between parts; its final assertion passes.
observations.child_impact: Stop-start movement can still progress, which may accommodate an unsteady finger. This does not establish that the timing or circle is comfortable for a child.
observations.proposed_repair: No repair indicated. Keep progress-preserving release behavior and validate physical stop-start play before tuning thresholds.
observations.acceptance_test: With ordinary touch on the target device, perform several short circular segments with natural lifts; verify partial grime remains, the child can resume, and completion requires continued intentional scrubbing.

observations.title: Finger ownership, busy release, and focus cancellation are covered in the scripted path
evidence: scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleaning.gd:548-590 (single touch ID ownership, ID-matched release, buffered press cleanup, and focus reset)

scripts/probe_day_one_bathroom_cleanup.gd:202-213,297-324; audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L03/attempt_1/probe.log:37-41,70-73 (second touch, focus-loss, buffered-release and held-buffer assertions pass)
observations.reproduction: The probe injects a second finger while the first owns the scrub, cancels during a partial gesture, and tests release versus hold during tool travel. All corresponding assertions pass.
observations.child_impact: The code path rejects the tested competing touch and prevents a released busy press from unexpectedly starting later. Actual device interruption and native focus behavior remain unverified; MA-TOUCH-001 still requires phone evidence.
observations.proposed_repair: No runtime change indicated. Obtain target-device hold, drag, second-finger, release, pause, and focus-loss evidence for this activity.
observations.acceptance_test: On the exact Android build, record an owned scrub, competing second finger, release during tool travel, app focus loss, pause, and resume; verify no stale scrub starts, ownership does not stick, and partial progress is retained.

observations.title: This PASS does not prove the child-facing bathroom entry or rendered scrub route
evidence: scripts/probe_day_one_bathroom_cleanup.gd:196-213,287-324 (local setup disables announcements and directly drives the cleaning object / gesture handler)
scripts/probe_day_one_bathroom_cleanup.gd:221-232,348-366 (test uses scripted gesture seams for completion and lift behavior)
observations.reproduction: Inspect probe setup and assertions: they instantiate the mechanic directly, suppress announcements, and use direct helper/input-handler calls; the receipt confirms headless scripted evidence only.
observations.child_impact: This run cannot show that a child reaches the sink stage, understands the circle cue, sees the scrub response at phone size, or hears the exact instruction.
observations.proposed_repair: No gameplay repair can be justified from this gap alone. Capture a routed fresh-entry session with actual sound and rendered output, then observe child discovery before adjusting the mechanic.
observations.acceptance_test: From a fresh save on the target phone, enter the bathroom through visible gameplay, hear and see the sink instruction, and perform a wobbly one-finger scrub; record the routed input, visible path, release/resume behavior, and child comprehension without coaching.

strengths.strength: Scrubbing exposes only the path under the moving tool, with unvisited grime preserved until the sink or tub gate completes.
The probe exercises intermittent touch, competing-finger rejection, release while busy, and focus cancellation; its unchanged run exits PASS with zero failed checks.

acceptance_gaps: The PASS is limited to the existing headless scripted probe at Godot 4.7.2-stable; it is not a routed visible-input or production visual acceptance (DL-QA-02, DL-QA-03).
No target-device touch geometry, latency, frame pacing, rendered cleanliness legibility, or audible voice evidence (DL-QA-04, DL-QA-07).
No observed child comprehension, comfort, discoverability, or fun evidence, and no owner review (DL-QA-05, DL-QA-06).
Fresh-save route proof remains open under MA-PLAY-001; exact spoken cue/playback evidence remains open under MA-ACCESS-001.
